objective: Remove obsolete 5 MiB photo caps across public/scoped Wall posts, anonymous Community posts, Marites stories, Dugtong, personal Connect photos and post edits; align every active and fallback media contract at 25 MiB while improving source fidelity and weak-network upload reliability without weakening media authorization or replacing the media engine.
chosenApproach: Raise the canonical per-photo limit to 20 MiB consistently in app and live database RPC validation; preserve already-encoded JPEGs up to the new limit; use a 2048px long-edge and quality 0.86 JPEG conversion only when conversion is required; route photo originals >=6 MiB through the existing TUS resumable uploader.
selectionRationale: Production evidence showed set_buklod_post_media_v7 delegates validation to v5, whose live definition still rejected photos above 5 MiB. The bucket is private with a 1 GiB limit. Supabase recommends TUS for uploads above 6 MiB and unstable networks. This aligns client, RPC and transport without altering ownership/scope authorization.
preserveBehaviors: Exact scope membership and path authorization
1 GiB video contract and AWS multipart route
Optional previews never block authoritative originals
TUS 6 MiB chunk size and bounded offset recovery
acceptanceChecks: Client photo limit is 25 MiB and matches production RPC validation
Existing JPEG bytes are preserved without unnecessary recompression
Converted images use 2048px maximum long edge and quality 0.86
Photo originals >=6 MiB use resumable TUS transport
v7 wrapper continues to delegate original media validation to v5
Focused tests, TypeScript, Performance QA, Engineering Accountability and integration QA pass
Production database migration is applied and queried after PR merge
Physical-device verification is skipped per user instruction
Community photo RPC fallbacks v1/v4/v5/v6 all accept 25 MiB; v1 supports the current 10-photo limit
Anonymous Community and Dugtong RPCs accept 25 MiB while preserving opaque path and owner checks
Personal direct-message RPC and private bucket both accept 25 MiB
alternativeApproaches: Remove all photo size limits (rejected: creates unbounded memory, egress and abuse risk).
Keep standard one-shot photo PUTs above 6 MiB (rejected: less reliable on weak mobile networks).
Change only the client limit (rejected: live v5 RPC would still reject valid uploads).
Replace image/video engines or expose public storage URLs (rejected: unnecessary and unsafe).
